examples.question_text: A network models water pipes connecting four storage tanks. Vertices represent tanks, edges represent pipes, and edge weights give pipe lengths in metres. What does an edge labelled $24$ between vertices $P$ and $Q$ represent?
examples.solution_text: A pipe connects tanks $P$ and $Q$. Its length is $24\text{ m}$.

a. Follow the arrows along $A\text{–}B\text{–}C\text{–}D$.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Time}&=4+3+5\\&=12\text{ minutes}\end{aligned}$

b. Count each journey along an edge, including the second journey from $A$ to $B$.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Time}&=4+3+5+2+4\\&=18\text{ minutes}\end{aligned}$
The supplied walk finishes at $B$, so it is not closed.

$\begin{aligned}\text{Time via }P&=7+9\\&=16\text{ minutes}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Time via }Q&=5+8\\&=13\text{ minutes}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Time saved}&=16-13\\&=3\text{ minutes}\end{aligned}$
The route $H\text{–}Q\text{–}S$ is faster by $3\text{ minutes}$.

Test the path $A\text{–}B\text{–}C\text{–}D$.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Distance}&=4+3+10\\&=17\text{ km}\end{aligned}$
A suitable path is $A\text{–}B\text{–}C\text{–}D$.

Use the total for the first route.
$\begin{aligned}12+x+15&=43\\27+x&=43\\x&=16\end{aligned}$

Substitute $x=16$ into the second route total.
$\begin{aligned}16+y+17&=50\\33+y&=50\\y&=17\end{aligned}$
The segment latencies are $x=16\text{ ms}$ and $y=17\text{ ms}$.

examples.question_text:
These are all the flight connections in a network. Each row gives the total flights available per day on that connection.

| Connection | Flights per day |
| --- | ---: |
| Sydney–Brisbane | 8 |
| Sydney–Melbourne | 12 |
| Sydney–Adelaide | 6 |
| Brisbane–Melbourne | 5 |

a. Find the total flights available per day across the network.
b. The maximum numbers of passengers who can depart Sydney daily for Brisbane, Melbourne and Adelaide are $960$, $1800$ and $720$, respectively. Find the maximum daily departures from Sydney.
examples.solution_text:
a. Count each connection once.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Total flights}&=8+12+6+5\\&=31\text{ flights per day}\end{aligned}$

b. Add the passenger capacities for the three connections departing Sydney.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Maximum departures}&=960+1800+720\\&=3480\text{ passengers per day}\end{aligned}$

a. Both candidate paths visit each required station once.
$\begin{aligned}\text{First path}&=12+16+14\\&=42\text{ km}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Second path}&=12+21+14\\&=47\text{ km}\end{aligned}$
The first candidate path, $A\text{–}B\text{–}C\text{–}D$, is shorter.

b. Include the return edge $DA$.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Closed tour distance}&=42+23\\&=65\text{ km}\end{aligned}$
